narrator.name: The Atlas narrator

narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Te Buki is a traditional dance form of Kiribati.
Its musical accompaniment is historically linked to the te kainikamaen, composers who were said to receive songs through myth or magic.
The dance has been documented in various islands, including Tabiteuea, Onotoa, and Nonouti, notably by Gerd Koch in 1963.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Te Buki is performed during formal occasions.
It is a distinct form of dance within the Kiribati tradition, separate from competitive, religious, or war-themed songs.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The primary instrument for te buki is the te orobaoki, a wooden box constructed to produce a hollow, reverberating tone.
The music is provided by a chorus of men who strike the box simultaneously.
Listen for the te orobaoki (wooden box).
A hollow, reverberating tone produced by a chorus of men striking a wooden box simultaneously.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Bata Teinamati is noted as one of Kiribati's most notable musicians.
The dance is performed across the islands of Kiribati, with documentation existing for performances in Tabiteuea, Onotoa, and Nonouti.
Te Buki is part of the broader Kiribati dance tradition, which includes the ruoia series, te kaimatoa, and various stick dances (tirere).

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.sound_description: A hollow, reverberating tone produced by a chorus of men striking a wooden box simultaneously.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Te Buki (Kiribati). Instruments: te orobaoki (wooden box). Vocal style: chanting or vocalizing. Mood: formal, reverberating. It should sound like this: A hollow, reverberating tone produced by a chorus of men striking a wooden box simultaneously. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.
